audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL and CL specifications: EOF container validation and execution (EIP-3540), deposit tree snapshots (EIP-4881), wallet signing with intended validator (EIP-7749), attestation aggregation optimization (EIP-7549), wallet chain addition (EIP-3085), Cancun VM jump destination validation, Istanbul hardfork gas repricing and precompiles (EIP-1679), DAO fork irregular state transition, BLS12-381 precompiles (EIP-2537), and IO-heavy opcode gas repricing (EIP-150).

in_scope: Precompiled Contracts (Blake2b EIP-152, BN128 EIP-1108, BLS12-381 EIP-2537)
Wallet RPC Methods (EIP-3085 chain addition, EIP-7749 signing)
Attestation Aggregation and Committee Index Optimization (EIP-7549)

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM execution context calling precompiles is an internal component, not an external entity. The actual external entity is the transaction sender or smart contract deployer.
EVM calldata is data passed within the system, not an external entity. The external source is the transaction sender providing the calldata.
Gas context is an internal EVM mechanism, not an external entity.
Generic 'attacker' is a threat actor, not a concrete external entity with a specific entry point. Attacker capabilities are modeled through other entities' trust levels.
Duplicate of EXT-DAPP with different intent. Trust model should use a single dApp entity with UNTRUSTED level rather than separate 'malicious' variant.
A calling contract within the EVM is an internal component. The external entity is the user/EOA that initiated the transaction.
SELFDESTRUCT beneficiary address is a parameter, not an external entity sending data into the system.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC (Transaction Sender)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit transactions including contract deployments with arbitrary bytecode (EOF or legacy). No authentication required on public JSON-RPC. Covers EXT-DEPLOYER, EXT-CALLER, EXT-TX-SENDER, and EXT-SMART-CONTRACT from subgraphs.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via Wallet JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps interact with wallets via injected provider JSON-RPC. Any website can call these methods. No authentication beyond browser origin. Covers EXT-DAPP from EIP-3085 and EIP-7749.

trusted_external_entities.name: Wallet User via UI
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Wallet confirmation dialog (approve/reject signing, chain addition)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Users may be socially engineered into approving malicious requests. While physically present, they cannot be trusted to make correct security decisions in all cases.

trusted_external_entities.name: Validator via P2P Gossip Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validators broadcast attestations over unauthenticated P2P gossip. Any peer can send attestations with potentially mutated committee indices. Covers EXT-VALIDATOR and EXT-P2P-PEER from EIP-7549.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Peer via Beacon API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers providing deposit tree snapshots may be malicious. Snapshot data must be cryptographically verified (Merkle root recalculation). No inherent trust in peer identity. Covers EXT-BEACON-PEER and EXT-SYNCING-CLIENT from EIP-4881.

trusted_external_entities.name: Prospective Validator via Deposit Contract
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit contract (32 ETH deposit transaction on EL, consumed by CL)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Anyone can submit deposits to the deposit contract. Deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal credentials, signature) is untrusted and must be validated by the CL. Covers EXT-VALIDATOR from EIP-4881.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers (miners in PoW era) propagate blocks over unauthenticated P2P. Blocks may contain invalid headers, incorrect extra_data markers, or attempt to violate fork rules. Covers EXT-BLOCK-PRODUCER from DAO fork.

trusted_external_entities.name: DAO Token Holder via Transaction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Token holders interact via standard transactions. The recovery contract must validate entitlement internally. No external trust.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Contract Deployment (CREATE/CREATE2 with EOF or legacy bytecode)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Full EOF container validation required: magic bytes, version, section order, type section size, code section count, container size <= MAX_INITCODE_SIZE, no stray bytes. All validation must be deterministic across clients.
Jump destination validation must prevent execution of PUSH data as opcodes. EOF opcode restrictions must be enforced. Gas costs must be correctly calculated per fork rules.
Full input validation required: length checks, field element encoding (top 16 bytes zero, value < modulus), curve membership, subgroup membership for MSM/pairing. Gas pricing must prevent DoS.
Chain ID format validation, RPC URL scheme validation (HTTPS only), chain ID match verification against RPC endpoint, user consent required. Must prevent TOCTOU attacks on chain ID.
Wallet must display validator address and data to user for approval. EIP-191 prefix (0x19 0x00) provides domain separation preventing cross-context signature reuse and transaction replay.
User must be shown complete and accurate information about the request. Wallet must not manipulate displayed data. However, user approval alone is insufficient - technical validation must also pass.

Committee membership must be verified before caching (pre-cache verification) to prevent gossip mutation attacks. BLS signature verification required. Attestation format must match post-fork (Electra) requirements.
Snapshot must be cryptographically verified: recalculate deposit root from finalized hashes and compare to transmitted root. Snapshot must be cross-checked against weak subjectivity checkpoint.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Deposit contract events (processed by CL from EL deposit logs)
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal credentials, amount, signature) must be validated. Merkle proof required for beacon chain inclusion. Deposit finalization requires both eth1_data finalization and deposit_index conditions.

Full header validation required: block number, timestamp, gas, difficulty, parent hash. During DAO fork window (10 blocks), extra_data must contain b'dao-hard-fork' marker. Fork activation rules must be applied deterministically.
Recovery contract must correctly calculate proportional share based on DAO token holdings. Must prevent double-withdrawal and unauthorized access.
